# Japan Festivals — Oct
Source: seasons.kooexperience.com | 7 events

## Tips
- Book accommodation months ahead for major festivals (Gion Matsuri, Nebuta, Sumida Fireworks)
- Fireworks season peaks July–August; winter events peak January–February

## 🎆 Fireworks (3)

### Tsuchiura All-Japan Fireworks (土浦全国花火競技大会)
- **When:** Oct — First Saturday of October
- **Location:** Ibaraki (Kanto)
- **Attendance:** ~500,000 visitors
- **Note:** Autumn fireworks competition — one of Japan's three major competitions alongside Nagaoka and Omagari. Held over Lake Kasumigaura.
- **Official site:** https://www.tsuchiura-hanabi.jp/
- **GPS:** 36.0867, 140.2036 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=36.0867,140.2036

### Atami Sea Fireworks (熱海海上花火大会)
- **When:** Feb, Apr, Jul, Aug, Oct, Dec — Multiple times per year (Feb, Apr, Jul, Aug, Oct, Dec)
- **Location:** Shizuoka (Kanto)
- **Attendance:** ~30,000 visitors
- **Note:** Unique: held year-round in Atami Bay. The bowl-shaped bay amplifies sound and creates a spectacular visual. Close to Tokyo — easy day trip.
- **Official site:** https://www.ataminews.gr.jp/
- **GPS:** 35.095, 139.0733 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=35.095,139.0733

### Lake Toya Long-Run Fireworks (洞爺湖ロングラン花火大会)
- **When:** Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct — Every night Apr 28 – Oct 31 at 8:45PM
- **Location:** Hokkaido (Hokkaido)
- **Attendance:** ~500 visitors
- **Note:** Japan's most unique fireworks — launched over Lake Toya every single night for 6 months. Small but intimate; can be seen from lakeside ryokan.
- **Official site:** https://toyako.biz/
- **GPS:** 42.5833, 140.8 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=42.5833,140.8

## 🏮 Matsuri (4)

### Takayama Autumn Festival (高山祭（秋）)
- **When:** Oct — October 9–10
- **Location:** Gifu (Chubu)
- **Attendance:** ~130,000 visitors
- **Note:** Autumn version of the Takayama festival — same spectacular floats but set against autumn foliage. Often considered the more beautiful of the two.
- **Official site:** https://www.hidatakayama.or.jp/
- **GPS:** 36.145, 137.2521 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=36.145,137.2521

### Jidai Matsuri (時代祭)
- **When:** Oct — October 22
- **Location:** Kyoto (Kansai)
- **Attendance:** ~120,000 visitors
- **Note:** One of Kyoto's three great festivals. 2,000 participants in historical costumes spanning 1,200 years of history march from Kyoto Imperial Palace to Heian Shrine.
- **Official site:** https://www.heianjingu.or.jp/
- **GPS:** 35.0282, 135.7822 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=35.0282,135.7822

### Kurama Fire Festival (鞍馬の火祭)
- **When:** Oct — October 22
- **Location:** Kyoto (Kansai)
- **Attendance:** ~20,000 visitors
- **Note:** One of Kyoto's most dramatic festivals. Villagers carry torches through the mountain village of Kurama at night. Same date as Jidai Matsuri — do both.
- **Official site:** https://www.yukijinjya.jp/
- **GPS:** 35.1208, 135.7698 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=35.1208,135.7698

### Nagasaki Kunchi (長崎くんち)
- **When:** Oct — October 7–9
- **Location:** Nagasaki (Kyushu)
- **Attendance:** ~700,000 visitors
- **Note:** Unique festival showing Nagasaki's Chinese and Dutch heritage — dragon dances, Dutch ship floats, and exotic performances at Suwa Shrine.
- **Official site:** https://www.nagasaki-kunchi.com/
- **GPS:** 32.7503, 129.8779 · https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=32.7503,129.8779
